Vestas Wind Systems A/S Reports Steady Trade Activity in Latest Figures

Vestas Wind Systems A/S, Denmark’s leading wind turbine manufacturer, released its latest trade figures on Thursday, showing continued stable activity in both domestic and international markets. The figures confirm the company’s ongoing role as a key participant in the global renewable energy supply chain, with no major deviations from previous quarters.

According to the data provided by Vestas, exports of wind turbine components and related technology remained consistent with last year’s levels. The company shipped a total of 1,450 megawatts (MW) worth of equipment in the first quarter of the year, aligning with market expectations and reflecting steady demand from utility-scale projects in Europe and Asia.

“Vestas Wind Systems A/S continues to execute on its order book as planned. Our logistics and production teams have maintained reliable delivery schedules despite ongoing supply chain normalization across the sector,” said Lars Mikkelsen, Head of Investor Relations at Vestas. He added, “There have been no material disruptions impacting our trade operations.”

Industry analysts highlighted that Vestas’ performance mirrors broader trends in Denmark’s renewable energy export sector. “The figures demonstrate resilience and sustained international interest in Danish wind technology,” commented Sara Holm, an energy market analyst at Nordica Research. “With the sector’s stable regulatory environment and continued investment in infrastructure, companies like Vestas are well positioned for gradual growth.”

The Danish Renewable Energy Association noted that the export of wind turbines and parts remains a pillar of the country’s trade activity, generating significant value for local suppliers and logistics firms. “Vestas’ consistent export levels help underpin job security and economic activity in key Danish ports, including Esbjerg and Aarhus,” said association spokesperson Rasmus Petersen.

Vestas Wind Systems A/S is scheduled to release its next quarterly update in August.
